title: Triage matrix: prioritize polyglot SDK requests across language coverage, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics for enterprise onramp
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: Create a reproducible triage matrix and intake process to prioritize incoming enterprise SDK and client-library requests. Focus areas: language coverage gaps (priority languages vs usage signal), authentication patterns (token rotation, delegated SSO, long-lived credentials, KMS/HSM integrations), and streaming ergonomics (resumability, reconnection/backpressure, client-side buffering and message ordering). Deliverables: a documented rubric for intake decisions, prioritized backlog with rationale and cost-estimates, short design proposals for the top 3 language+feature combos, and a rollout plan including documentation and acceptance tests for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Rubric doc published in Confluence that scores requests on security risk, infra cost, customer impact, engineering effort, and time-to-value
Inventory mapping of the last 120 days of SDK requests to rubric scores with top-10 prioritized items
Low-fidelity SDK pattern proposals for two streaming auth workflows (token rotation + SSO handshake) and one resumable-stream design for JS and Python
Stakeholder signoff from Eng leads (runtime + SDK infra), Security, and Solutions by 2026-03-20
An ingestion template for new SDK requests (customer, repro, desired UX, compliance constraints) added to intake form and linked in the rubric
comments: 2026-03-01 — Ava Martinez: Kickoff — compiled customer request exports from Support and Solutions: ~62 SDK requests in past quarter (languages: JS 38%, Python 27%, Go 12%, Java 9%, other 14%). Initial hypothesis: prioritize resumable streaming and token rotation across JS/Python, then expand language coverage for Go/Java if consumption signal persists.

2026-03-03 — Liam Chen: Added engineering feasibility notes after sync with SDK infra: token rotation pattern is medium effort (4-6 points) because we need client-side token refresh hooks + server token-refresh endpoints; resumable streaming has high platform surface (stateful reconnect + KV cache compatibility) estimated 8-13 points.

2026-03-05 — Security (Maya Patel): Flagged KMS/HSM integration as high compliance risk for regulated customers; recommend separate track with security review and extra testing when customer_impact is high.

2026-03-07 — Solutions (Diego Alvarez): Customer beta candidates identified (3 customers) willing to test JS resumable-stream + token-rotation; would require a private Dedicated environment for initial validation.

2026-03-09 — Liam Chen: Decision log — scope MVP to: (1) token rotation SDK helpers + best-practice doc for JS/Python, (2) a resumable-stream reference in JS with a toggled server-side fallback; defer multi-language resumable-streams until after telemetry from beta. Reason: balance time-to-value for customers who hit token-expiry UX and reduce upfront platform changes.

2026-03-10 — Ava Martinez: Updated acceptance criteria and created intake template. Next steps: draft Confluence rubric, schedule cross-functional review (PM/Eng/Security/Solutions) for 2026-03-15. Added dependency on ENG-1842 for instrumentation hooks.
